verdict.rationale: Omarchy provides easy setup of dev environments via its Install > Development menu, includes VSCode, Cursor, Zed, Sublime, Helix, plus AI agent harnesses (OpenCode, Claude Code), showing support for modern IDEs and AI tooling on Arch Linux. However, it's a niche Arch-based distro rather than a mainstream 'primary supported platform,' and community evidence raises concerns about security, supply-chain risk (chaotic.cx repo, AUR-like plugin ecosystem) and stability that could undermine reliable use of the latest toolchains.
